evidence: Reviewed staged diff in MyAccessibilityService.kt: added an adaptive Picap event throttle at the top of onAccessibilityEvent - picapEventAllowed() maintains a 1-second sliding window over every Picap event arrival (including discarded ones), enters throttled mode when a window exceeds PICAP_FLOOD_HIGH (8 events/s), processes at most one Picap event per PICAP_THROTTLE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS (1000 ms) while throttled, and exits back to full processing only when a complete window falls to PICAP_FLOOD_LOW (4 events/s or fewer), logging both transitions and the number of discarded events; non-Picap events are completely unaffected; build.gradle.kts version bump to 0.3.44
aapt dump badging reports com.example.projectacc versionCode 59 versionName 0.3.44; compileDebugKotlin succeeded with no new warnings

findings.claim: Flood detection uses a 1-second window with enter above 8 events/s and exit at or below 4 events/s, giving hysteresis that prevents flapping between states; both transitions emit a single Log.i with the rate and drop count. A sustained rate between 5 and 8 events/s after a flood would keep the throttle active indefinitely because it never crosses the exit threshold, and a bursty pattern (quiet second then flood) will log an exit/enter pair per cycle; both outcomes are functionally safe because throttled processing still runs once per second and every transition is visible in logcat, and the thresholds are named constants that can be tuned per device.
proof_refs: picapEventAllowed evaluates exit only at window rollover using the completed window count before resetting picapFloodCount
enter check runs after every increment so a burst triggers throttling mid-window without waiting for rollover

findings.claim: Throttled Picap events return before the EVENT_DEBUG log and logWindows() dump, which is the intended load reduction; discarded events produce no per-event log line to avoid replacing the flood with a log flood, so visibility during throttling is limited to the entry/exit Log.i messages and the drop count they carry. The throttle check reads event.packageName before the existing null checks, so a null event or null package falls through to the original code path unchanged. The WhatsApp and system-package paths are byte-for-byte untouched, and the Picap pipeline is tree-re-read based (handlePicapEvent calls findAllWindows) so dropping intermediate events cannot lose state - only detection latency, bounded by the 1000 ms interval, changes.
proof_refs: guard condition event?.packageName?.toString() == PACKAGE_PICAP && !picapEventAllowed() placed as first statement of onAccessibilityEvent
handlePicapEvent starts with findAllWindows(PACKAGE_PICAP) and parses the fresh tree rather than the event payload
